resources.string: Where Pley listens for browsers and apps. Changes apply at once, and Pley keeps them in %1$s.
For a reverse proxy on this computer that serves Pley with HTTPS (Caddy, nginx, IIS), or for Pley on its own.
This computer and the networks chosen
Devices on those networks reach Pley at this computer\'s address there.
Those that come later too: another Wi-Fi, a VPN.
For Jellyfin apps such as Infuse.
The Jellyfin-compatible API\'s port is a number from 1 to 65535.
Choose another port for the Jellyfin-compatible API, or Pley\'s port.
For tools such as Kometa and Tautulli.
The Plex-compatible API\'s port is a number from 1 to 65535.
Choose another port for the Plex-compatible API, or Pley\'s port.
On a port of its own
The port is a number from 1 to 65535.
The Jellyfin-compatible and Plex-compatible APIs can\'t share a port.
Choose a network, or Only this computer.
Bonjour\'s host name is letters, digits and hyphens, 63 at most, not starting or ending with a hyphen.
Not on this computer now: Pley listens there once it is.
Set by --bind or PLEY_BIND, on the command line or in the environment: change it there.
Windows Firewall decides which kinds of network reach Pley: Pley\'s Setup lets it through on private and domain networks, unless you chose otherwise there (run Setup again to change that).
The web app\'s and the Pley apps\'.
On networks only: devices can\'t reach this computer\'s own address.
The Pley apps on these networks find this server by themselves.
Turned off by --no-bonjour, --no-discovery, PLEY_NO_BONJOUR or PLEY_NO_DISCOVERY.
Off unless turned on. Apple\'s devices find this server by it; without it, they need its address.
Where Apple\'s devices reach Pley; %1$s.local when left empty. They list it by the server\'s name (Settings → Server).
With a VPN, a virtual machine\'s or container\'s network, or a guest Wi-Fi, choose the networks whose devices should find Pley. Each network is told only Pley\'s address on it.
Those that come later too. 100.64.x.x ones (Tailscale) only when chosen.
Not a network Pley listens on now: announced there once it is.
Pley retries addresses it can\'t listen on yet every 30 seconds.
Pley listens on %1$s, which this page shows as near as it can: saving replaces them.
Saved: Pley listens on the rest once it can
Pley would stop listening where this phone reaches it: the phone couldn\'t reach it any more.
Stop listening where this phone reaches Pley?

Some proxies pass the address on without its port (nginx\'s $host, Nginx Proxy Manager). Pley then names itself without the port, and apps refuse it. Add the addresses with a port Pley is reached at that way, or have the proxy pass the port (proxy_set_header Host $http_host;).
